text.p: Recently volatile metal markets calmed down but Chicago grain markets remained sensitive to weather reports in commodity markets overnight.
LME activity was low-key on Thursday afternoon as metals gingerly explored new ranges in the aftermath of zinc's steep fall, traders said.
Three months zinc finished the afternoon kerb at exactly the same price as the previous day's close of $1,460 per tonne.
Traders seemed relieved that a whole day passed without any major jolts after prices dived $300 on Tuesday from seven-year highs and lurched up and down on Wednesday.
Prices found support in the morning around $1,420/30, then climbed in the afternoon to about $1,470.
The spreads narrowed, with the cash/threes failing to match Wednesday's $130 backwardation. It traded at a $90 backwardaton in the morning and finished the afternoon kerb bid at $75.
Aluminium got a foothold above the $1,700 level in the afternoon, but failed to sustain higher numbers on modest but persistent selling. It ended the day $4 firmer at $1,701.
Copper also explored higher numbers in the afternoon after finding support below $2,300 in the morning. Three months turned back, however, at around $2,325/30 and ended the day $13 firmer at $2,318.
The market appeared to be going through a consolidation phase, but most traders were betting on lower number as stocks continued to build.

Nickel popped higher, but failed to depart from its range, ending the day $70 firmer at $7,430. But after failing to break above its downtrend line at $7,580 on Wednesday and being hit by bank selling, lower levels were expected eventually.
Lead and tin barely moved the whole day, with lead ending unchanged at $732 and tin down $5 at $5,545.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures managed a higher close Thursday, with the exception of gold which continued to prove the weakest link in the complex. COMEX December gold ended down $2.00 at $328.60 an ounce, with the precious metal trading in increasingly narrower ranges in the past 10 days, after recovering partially from 12 year lows in the bullion market around $314.60 in early July. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $324.30/80, compared with the London Thursday afternoon fix at $326.35 and the New York close Wednesday at $325.80/30.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher on a rally in corn and soybean futures, traders said.

USDA's weekly export sales report was supportive. USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat during the week ended July 24 totalled 964,300 tonnes, above expectations for 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes. Reports from the U.S. spring wheat tour indicating yield prospects below the year ago and below the average rate also may have provided some support.
Wheat closed 2-1/2 to 5-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with September up 5-3/4 at $3.62.

NYMEX crude retraced its heaviest losses of the session Thursday afternoon after a trading house sought to bid crude up in light volume, dealers said. September crude ended 16 cents a barrel lower at $20.14 a barrel after falling to $19.65 early session.
